items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: there was an old man and his name was Mr. Warwick (PHONETIC). He was playing a C melody saxophone.

ctx.x: on and study piano. He took me to his piano teacher, a lady named Josephine Guy, that's right. And I started studying piano and practicing on his piano because we didn't have a piano at home. I studied piano about a year and was doing pretty good. But the kids in the neighborhood started calling me a sissy because I was playing piano so I didn't want to play the piano, I gave it up. And one day Merle came over to my house and said, they're organizing a community band. And they're going to furnish the instruments…

Well, to please him I went along with him. We went to this meeting and when we got there there was an old man and his name was Mr. Warwick (PHONETIC). He was playing a C melody saxophone. And I had never seen a saxophone before to notice it. And I said, what instrument is that? He said, 'that's a saxophone, C melody.' I said, 'well, that's the instrument I'd like to play.'

So I signed up for saxophone. Well, this orchestra never did materialize, we never did get the instruments or anything. But I had made up my mind that I wanted to be a saxophone player so I told my mother --
